source: Intel rows: Intel ARK SKU pages that list the exact Device ID; max_threads is the largest Total Threads of any SKU read that lists it. AMD rows: the device id gives the APU family (pci-ids), max_threads is the highest 'Total Threads / # of Threads' of an AMD SKU of that family.
note: Same method as intel-gen9-thread-caps.json with one difference: no walk is complete. Each row's `walk` field says what was not read. An unread SKU can only raise a cap, so a cap here is a lower bound: a claim within it is backed by a real SKU, a real part may have more. Intel ids and AMD ids are separate namespaces (key = vendor + id). Pages were read by lookup agents; every Intel source_url was re-fetched (the page is the named SKU); re-read from the page text: Device ID of 0xA7A8, 0x46A3, 0x9A78, 0x4692, 0x7D67, 0x7D51, Total Threads of 0x7D67 and 0x7D51, and for all 7 AMD rows the SKU page's '# of Threads' and 'Former Codename' (amd.com). The other Intel Total Threads and Device ID lines and the pci-ids family lines are the lookup agents' quotes, not re-read. Ids that never occur in BrowserForge 1.2.4's Windows Chrome renderers (0x8A51, 0x8A5C) were left out. Rows with max_threads null are unsourced and never drawn.
